newsitem.title: UK: Moscow eyes second Eurobond if debut well-received.
newsitem.headline: Moscow eyes second Eurobond if debut well-received.

text.p: Moscow will consider launching a second Eurobond this year if its upcoming Eurobond is well-received, a Moscow official told bankers on Thursday.
"If we are successful then we will consider doing a second debt issue," chairman of the committee for municipal loans & stock market Mechislav Klimovich said.
Moscow is expected to launch a three-year Eurobond of between $300 and $400 million before the end of May.
Klimovich said Moscow was limited to raise $500 million this year.
He said Moscow's ratings of Ba2 by Moody's Investors Service and BB- by Standard & Poor's were constrained by the sovereign ceiling.
"Moscow's intrinsic credit fundamentals are not fully reflected by its ratings," he said.
Meanwhile the mayor of the City of Moscow Yuri Luzhkov was not part of its delegation which addressed investors on Thursday.

Deputy mayor of Moscow Valeri Shantsev said Luzhkov -- who was also due to address bankers at a conference in London on Friday -- had matters to attend to in Moscow, among other things a mayoral forum.
Luzhkov was due to deliver an address on "Moscow on the Edge of the 21st Century" as well as host a panel discussion at the conference on Friday.
Organisers of the conference Sachs Associates were unable to immediately comment on Luzhkov's unexpected absence.
